title: Plasmid Sequence Analysis from Long Reads
author: David A Eccles

steps.title: Download required bioinformatics scripts
steps.instruction: Clone the necessary helper scripts from the provided GitLab repository.

substeps.instruction: Run: git clone https://gitlab.com/gringer/bioinfscripts.git scripts

steps.title: Demultiplex Nanopore reads
steps.instruction: Demultiplex reads using LAST or MinKNOW to create the required input format.

substeps.instruction: If using LAST: Follow the 'Demultiplexing Nanopore reads with LAST' protocol.

If using MinKNOW: Create a 'demultiplexed' directory and run a loop to cat fastq files from the readLocation (e.g., ../*/fastq_pass or ../*/pass for Guppy), gzip them into demultiplexed/reads_${x}.fq.gz, and record the barcodes in barcode_counts.txt.

steps.title: Prepare results directory
steps.instruction: Create a directory to store the output files.

substeps.instruction: cd demultiplexed
mkdir results

steps.title: Determine plasmid length
steps.instruction: Identify the plasmid length if not previously known using L50 summary statistics.

substeps.instruction: Run: scripts/fastx-length.pl reads_BC05.fq.gz > /dev/null

steps.title: Set reference sequence variable
steps.instruction: Define the reference sequence name and ensure the file is located at reference/refName.fa.

substeps.instruction: Export the variable: export REFNAME="refName" (replace 'refName' with the actual sequence name).

steps.title: Create LAST index for reference
steps.instruction: Generate a LAST index for the reference sequence.

substeps.instruction: Run: lastdb -uNEAR -R01 reference/${REFNAME}.fa reference/${REFNAME}.fa

steps.title: Prepare substitution matrix
steps.instruction: Create a substitution matrix (plasmid.mat) for barcode mapping, incorporating quality scores.

substeps.instruction: Train LAST using: last-train --matsym -Q 1 -P 10 reference/${REFNAME}.fa Filtered_reads_BC*.fastq.gz
Copy the last few lines of the output into a text file named 'plasmid.mat'.

steps.title: Map reads to reference
steps.instruction: Map reads to the reference sequence and convert the output to sorted BAM format.

substeps.instruction: For each barcode in barcode_counts.txt, run a pipeline: lastal -j 7 -P 10 -p plasmid.mat reference/${REFNAME}.fa Filtered_reads_{bc}.fastq.gz | last-split -n -m 0.99 | last-postmask | maf-convert sam | samtools view -h --reference reference/${REFNAME}.fa | samtools sort > results/${bc}_vs_${REFNAME}.bam
Index the resulting BAM files: samtools index results/${bc}_vs_${REFNAME}.bam

steps.title: Split and tally base counts
steps.instruction: Separate reads into forward and reverse-mapped sequences and calculate base counts at each location.

substeps.instruction: For each barcode, extract forward reads (samtools view -b -F 0x10) and reverse reads (samtools view -b -f 0x10), pipe through samtools mpileup --reference reference/${REFNAME}.fa -B -Q 0 -, and process with ~/scripts/readstomper.pl -c to generate .csv files in the results folder.

steps.title: Visualize base-stomped output
steps.instruction: Generate a visualization plot of the stomped output for each barcode.

substeps.instruction: Run: ~/scripts/stomp_plotter.r -f results/fwd_stomped_${bc}_vs_${REFNAME}.csv -r results/rev_stomped_${bc}_vs_${REFNAME}.csv -prefix results/${bc}

steps.title: Perform Canu assembly
steps.instruction: Run a Canu assembly on each read set using default options and the determined plasmid length.

substeps.instruction: Run: canu -nanopore Filtered_reads_${bc}.fq.gz -p ${bc} -d results/canu_${bc} genomeSize=${plasmidLength}

steps.title: Trim assembled contigs
steps.instruction: Trim the longest assembled contig based on Canu's trim recommendations.

substeps.instruction: Use samtools faidx and grep to identify trim coordinates, then process through scripts/fastx-fetch.pl, scripts/fastx-sort.pl -l, and scripts/fastx-fetch.pl -c 1 to produce results/longest_circTrimmed_${bc}.fasta.

steps.title: Orient sequences by polyA region
steps.instruction: If a long polyA region is present, orient the assembled sequences assuming the longest homopolymer is the polyA region.

substeps.instruction: Check for 'T' using scripts/fastx-hplength.pl; if found, use scripts/fastx-rc.pl and scripts/fastx-fetch.pl -oneline to create results/oriented_longest_circTrimmed_${bc}.fasta; otherwise, use scripts/fastx-fetch.pl -oneline directly.

steps.title: Orient plasmid by alignment sequence
steps.instruction: Rotate the plasmid based on a known alignment sequence.

substeps.instruction: Create alignment sequence file: echo -e ">align_seq\nGAGACGGTCGACTGCGGCCGCTCGAGTCT" > align_seq.fa
Index the sequence: lastdb -uRY4 -R01 align_seq.fa align_seq.fa

Determine rotation and rotate: scripts/fastx-rotate.pl -o $(lastal align_seq.fa results/oriented_longest_circTrimmed_${bc}.fasta | grep BC | awk '{print $3}') results/oriented_longest_circTrimmed_${bc}.fasta > results/rotated_longest_circTrimmed_${bc}.fasta
